source.title: Are neural scaling laws leading quantum chemistry astray?

record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling behavior in quantum-chemistry models and argues from its own results that scaling does not ensure reliable physical generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out test-set error trends, H2 bond-dissociation predictions, and foundation-model energy curves. Background claims about scaling from cited work are not recorded as results. Foundation-model curve evaluations are recorded as findings about physical generalization, not as evidence of a scale trend: the paper does not analyze those models' performance against model size.
record.test_reason: The authors train SchNet regressors on molecular-energy data across six capacities and several training-set sizes. They report test-set error versus scale (bears on V5) and whether out-of-distribution H2 dissociation predictions improve with scale (bears on V6). They argue from their own results that scaling is insufficient.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors attribute the modest VQM24 improvement to exposure to dissociated structures, not to learning underlying physics. They warn that large models may act as data-driven interpolators. Even AIMNet2, which has an explicit Coulomb term, fails the two-proton test.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SchNet and pretrained molecular interatomic potentials to predict molecular energies, rather than language models trained and evaluated with held-out cross-entropy. Studies chemistry test error and extrapolation to molecular bond curves; it does not measure language-model compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset composition changes H2 extrapolation: VQM24 includes saddle-point/off-equilibrium structures and yields modestly more realistic curves than stable-only GDB-9-G4(MP2).

fits_no_version.finding: Foundation interatomic potentials (6.3M–1.4B parameters) fail qualitatively on non-H2 diatomics and predict two bare protons as bound by ~500 kcal/mol. The paper gives no analysis by size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large pretrained interatomic potentials can violate basic physics (Coulomb repulsion, dissociation shape) regardless of size or data diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: Training data that includes off-equilibrium (saddle-point) structures, as in VQM24, yields H2 curves that roughly resemble the reference. Stable-only data (GDB-9) yields flat curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Out-of-distribution generalization of molecular models depends on training-data coverage more than on scale.

record.problems: The scaling curves are presented in figures without numerical values or reported uncertainty. The H2 and foundation-model physical-generalization results are mainly qualitative; the paper does not quantify scale-to-performance trends for the foundation models.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured.
No small-run fits are used to predict larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation between model size and data is studied.
Depth and width are varied only through capacity c=d×w; there is no comparison of shapes at fixed parameter count.
No fitted exponents are reported. The data range is about 10^2 to 5·10^5 samples. Compute scaling, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
No standard downstream benchmarks are used. Performance is not related to pretraining loss. No scale trend is analysed for the foundation models.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Effect of model capacity on test MAE: 'Larger model capacities generally reduce errors'. This is the parameter-scaling side of V5 and has no row.

record.verdict_notes: The V6 linkage is a stretch. The task is out-of-distribution extrapolation by supervised molecular regressors, not language-model downstream benchmarks, so weigh the V6 'challenges' labels accordingly. UMA-S (150M) and UMA-M (1.4B) share training data and could give a size comparison, but the paper does not analyse it. All scaling evidence is figure-only, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy or its dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model size and training tokens is studied.
Depth and width configurations are used, but the paper does not test how architecture shape affects loss at fixed parameter count.

Tests held-out molecular-energy prediction error against training-set size and model capacity; does not test other modalities beyond chemistry, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or power-law fits across several orders of magnitude.
Tests SchNet extrapolation to H2 bond-dissociation curves across capacities and datasets, but not standard language-model downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
The paper does not compare fitted exponents, fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, or compute-optimal allocations.
